summary: Set up a local Ubuntu package repository on node1 (flat repo at /srv/local-repo, indexed with dpkg-scanpackages, served via a systemd-managed python3 http.server on $NODE_IP:8080), blocked the remote archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com repos at the network layer with iptables/ip6tables REJECT rules and disabled their apt source, then installed the hello package purely from the local repo and confirmed it runs. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and service/package health, rebooted node1, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the local-repo service, installed package, and apt functionality against the local repo all recovered post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (Ubuntu 24.04) and apt configuration
Installed dpkg-dev and downloaded hello_2.10-3build1_amd64.deb into /srv/local-repo/pool while remotes were still reachable
Built repo metadata with dpkg-scanpackages, placed Packages/Packages.gz at repo root for flat-repo format
Served the repo via python3 http.server bound to $NODE_IP:8080, then converted it to a systemd unit (local-repo-http.service) for persistence
Resolved archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com to their IPv4/IPv6 addresses and blocked outbound tcp/80,443 to them via iptables/ip6tables REJECT rules
Verified remote repos became unreachable (curl connection failures) while local repo remained reachable
Disabled /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources (renamed to .disabled) and added local-repo.list apt source
Ran apt-get update successfully against only the local repo, then installed and ran the hello package from it
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, service state, package state, repo HTTP reachability, firewall rule count)
Issued sudo reboot on node1 with acknowledgement returned before disconnect, polled until command execution resumed
Confirmed boot_id changed from a0c36ad2-af0d-42fe-ad6f-4750699390c2 to bb0545c0-22ff-4d7b-9a8b-43a9251eb862
Verified post-reboot recovery: local-repo-http.service active, hello package installed and executable, repo HTTP reachable, apt-get update against local repo succeeded

evidence.requirement: Remote repositories confirmed reachable at baseline before being made unreachable
evidence.summary: apt-cache show hello succeeded and curl to archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com returned HTTP 200 before any blocking was applied

evidence.requirement: Local package repository built from local storage and served
evidence.summary: hello .deb downloaded to /srv/local-repo/pool, dpkg-scanpackages generated Packages/Packages.gz, and python3 http.server confirmed listening on $NODE_IP:8080 serving the Packages file

evidence.requirement: Remote repositories made genuinely unreachable (network-level, not just config)
evidence.summary: iptables/ip6tables REJECT rules added for all resolved archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com addresses on ports 80/443; curl afterward failed to connect (exit 7) to both hosts

evidence.requirement: apt configured to use only the local repo and successfully update against it
evidence.summary: ubuntu.sources disabled, local-repo.list added pointing at http://$NODE_IP:8080, and apt-get update completed (exit 0) fetching Packages only from the local repo

evidence.requirement: Package installed from the local repository while remotes were unreachable, and functions correctly
evidence.summary: apt-get install -y hello fetched the package solely from http://10.100.2.10:8080, installed it, and running `hello` printed 'Hello, world!'

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id (a0c36ad2-...), active local-repo-http.service, installed hello package, reachable repo HTTP endpoint, and hello execution prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restarted with safe reboot mechanism, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: sudo reboot issued via backgrounded nohup so the ack returned immediately; next exec call confirmed connection reset, proving the node went down

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proven after restart
evidence.summary: cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id returned bb0545c0-22ff-4d7b-9a8b-43a9251eb862, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, confirming an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and data verified
evidence.summary: After reboot: local-repo-http.service active, hello package still installed and runnable, repo HTTP endpoint reachable, and apt-get update against the local repo succeeded
